title: Berlin Attraction Tickets - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin sells its famous list through three different doors, and the search page never tells you which one you are in.** Some sights have no ticket at all, two of the best are free but only the venue can reserve them, and a short list has a real price.

**Five of the most-visited places in central Berlin have no admission and no booking:** the Brandenburg Gate, the East Side Gallery, Topography of Terror, the Berlin Wall Memorial at Bernauer Straße and the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe. There is nothing to buy at any of them.

**The Reichstag dome is free, and only the Bundestag can put you on the list.** You register every visitor's name and date of birth in advance, and everyone from 16 shows an original passport or identity card at the door. Copies are refused.
**The Jewish Museum core exhibition is free for everyone,** with a time-slot ticket from the museum itself. Its temporary exhibitions cost 10 euros.
**The whole paid half of a classic Berlin list comes to 93.90 euros for one adult:** Museum Island 24, TV Tower from 20, Berliner Dom 15, DDR Museum 13.90, Charlottenburg Palace 12, Humboldt Forum 9.

**Skip-the-line is narrower than it sounds.** The TV Tower's own standard ticket skips the ticket desk line and says in the same sentence that the admission line still applies. Only a timed slot removes the second queue.
**At the DDR Museum the online price and the door price are both 13.90 euros,** so booking ahead buys you time, never money.

**Before paying, check the domain.** Berlin venues sell from their own names: tv-turm.de, shop.berlinerdom.de, ddr-museum.de, humboldtforum.org, tickets.spsg.de, shop.smb.museum, visite.bundestag.de. A booking fee appearing at checkout means you are in a shop, not at the venue.
**Prices and rules here were read from each venue's own website on 23 August 2026.**
